summary: Andreas Gottlieb Hoffmann was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle under Wilhelm Gesenius (Ph.D. ~1814–1820) and held posts at Halle (1822) and the University of Jena (Professor of Theology, 1826).
Andreas N. Kephallenos was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies at the University of Florence and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Munich.

Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Munich (~1856–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1860–1861), later teaching Albert Grünwedel.

Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol. Messent studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams as well as teachers Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

Andrei Vostrikov was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Boris Vladimirtsov. He held posts at the Asiatic Museum, Institute of Buddhist Culture, and University of Chicago (1924–1937).

Andrej Evgen’evič Snesarev was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University and the General Staff Academy, later heading the General Staff Academy (1919) and Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1922–1924).
Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University. In 2009, he was attested as an Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College.

Andrew Garrett is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1985–1990). In 1995, he took up a post at the University of California, Berkeley as professor of linguistics and acting director of the survey.

Andrew Glass is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard G. Salomon), also studying under Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, and others.

Andrew Goudie is a history and archaeology scholar who completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Trinity Hall (1964–1970). He subsequently served as Head and Professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Andrew Henry Yarrow was an Indology scholar who studied at UNC Chapel Hill and Yale University (Ph.D. ~1946–1950 under Franklin Edgerton). He held posts at Yale (~1950–1951), Columbia University (1952), and the University of Miami.

Andrew Hollingworth Frost was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at St John's College (1838–1842). He served as Principal of Church Missionary Society College, Islington (1870–1874) and Lecturer in Marathi and Gujarati at Cambridge (1884–1902).

Andrew J. Nicholson is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied under Shrinarayan Mishra. He held posts as Senior Fellow at the University of Chicago (attested 2013) and Associate Professor at Stony Brook University (attested 2016–2026).
Andrew Jukes was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who was educated at Blundell's School. He served as a medical missionary for the Church Mission Society from 1878 to 1906.

Andrew O. Fort is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Amherst College and the University of Pennsylvania (~1976–1982). He served as an Associate Professor at Texas Christian University from ~1982 to 2021.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (2014).

Andrew Ollett is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Oxford (~2008–2010) and Columbia University (~2011–2017). He became an Associate Professor at the University of Chicago around 2020.

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University, with teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Harvard and Yale University (under Warren Crawford Cowgill, ~1963–1967). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1967.
